{{Short description|Indian American mathematician (1944/1945–2023)}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=December 2023}}
{{Indian name|Lakshmibai|Venkatraman}}
'''Venkatramani Lakshmibai''' (1944 – 2 December 2023) was an Indian mathematician who was a professor of mathematics at [[Northeastern University]] in Boston. Her research concerned [[algebraic geometry]], the theory of [[algebraic group]]s, and [[representation theory]],{{r|profile}} including in particular the theory of [[Generalized flag variety|flag varieties]] and [[Schubert variety|Schubert varieties]].

Lakshmibai was born in 1944 in a small town in southern [[India]].{{r|mom}} She earned her PhD in 1976 from the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]]{{r|profile}} under the direction of [[C. S. Seshadri]].{{r|mathgen}} She left India to teach in Europe and then in the United States, where she was a professor at Northeastern University from 1987 to 2019.{{r|mom}} With [[Sara Billey]] she was the co-author of the monograph ''Singular Loci of Schubert Varieties'' (Progress in Mathematics 182, Birkhäuser, 2000).{{r|brion}} She also co-authored two monographs with Justin Brown: ''Flag Varieties: An Interplay of Geometry, Combinatorics, and Representation Theory'' (Texts and Readings in Mathematics 53, Hindustan Book Agency, 2009){{r|ohn}} and ''The Grassmannian Variety: Geometric and Representation-Theoretic Aspects'' (Developments in Mathematics 42, Springer, 2015).{{r|lili}}

In 2012 she was selected as one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].{{r|fams}}

Lakshmibai died on 2 December 2023, at the age of 78.{{r|died}}
